statement: For every field K and all integers n,m>=2, if I_{n,m}=NI(B(n,m)^3) is the closed-neighborhood ideal defined in source.md and interpreted in problem.md, then pd_S(S/I_{n,m})=floor(m/4)+1, reg_S(S/I_{n,m})=n+m-1-floor(m/4), and ht(I_{n,m})=floor(m/7)+1. Consequently S/I_{n,m} is Cohen--Macaulay exactly when m is 2, 3, or 7 (for every n>=2). There are no exceptional small-m values outside these uniform formulas.
contribution: A complete characteristic-free solution of the frozen original problem. The proof derives exact minimal mapping-cone recurrences from three explicit monomial colon identities, proves mapping-cone minimality by a new-variable multigrading, solves every base case and residue class, and proves height by matching vertex-cover upper and packing lower bounds. Exact Singular computations provide boundary checks but are not used as proof. No claim of bibliographic priority is made beyond the limited nearest-source comparison in problem.md.
